title: Partner SKU governance and creative quick sheets
content:
Purpose:
Quick, actionable reference for packaging partner SKUs and creative assets for cloud marketplaces (AWS/Azure/GCP) — focused on minimizing back-and-forth during listing submission and reducing rejection risk. Use as a producer checklist + copy bank for sellers and internal ops reviewers.

Context/why this lives: 
- We see repeated rework around SKU descriptions, trial entitlements, and image ratios.
- Legal and marketplace compliance flags come late and block publication.
- This doc is a compact set of canonical fields, short-copy variants, image/asset specs, and an acceptance QA matrix to speed review cycles.

How to use: 
1) Seller or partner rep fills the SKU brief (section A) and attaches required assets.
2) Creative owner picks copy variant and prepares images per spec.
3) Ops runs the acceptance QA matrix (section C).
4) If green, staging publish; if not, annotate JIRA and follow rollback/contingency notes.

A. SKU Brief (fields we require from partner / internal product team)
- product_name_short: 6–8 words, no trademark punctuation. Example: "Redwood Inference Dedicated GPU Pool"
- product_name_long: 12–18 words, allowed to include colon. Example: "Redwood Inference — Dedicated GPU Pools for Low-latency LLM Serving and Predictable Throughput"
- one_line_tag: 8–12 words, value-first. Example: "Predictable, production-grade LLM inference with reserved GPUs and SLA-backed latency"
- core_features (bulleted): 3–5; single-line each; avoid marketing hyperbole (no "best", "fastest" unless benchmarked)
- ideal_customer_profile: 1–2 short sentences (who buys this?)
- entitlement/trial: explicit list: e.g., "14-day trial, 50k tokens, up to 2 dedicated instances" or "no trial"
- pricing_hint: string (e.g., "usage + monthly reservation; contact sales for enterprise")
- technical_footprint: cpu/gpu counts, region availability, required VPC settings (if Private)
- privacy_compliance_flags: GDPR/PIPEDA/HIPAA?: yes/no + notes
- customer_data_handling: short note, e.g., "no customer prompts retained beyond 30d; KMS integrated"
- partner_contacts: name/email/role (single-line, comma-separated)
- assets_attached: list filenames (tile.png, hero-16x9.jpg, spec-sheet.pdf)

B. Short copy bank (pick 1 per field; prioritize 1 or 2 variants per marketplace)
1) 50-character headline examples:
- "Dedicated inference for production LLMs"
- "Predictable LLM latency with reserved GPUs"
2) 100–140 char description variants:
- Variant A (technical): "Reserved GPU pools and autoscaling for low-latency LLM inference. SLA-backed throughput with monitoring and KV-cache optimization."
- Variant B (business): "Ship feature-rich LLM experiences with predictable cost and performance. Fast on-ramps for dev teams + enterprise controls."
3) 280–350 char full tile text (for marketplace long descriptions):
- Tech-focused (example): "Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Features include reserved GPU pools, automatic KV/prefix caching, cost-aware batching, and rollout controls for safe model updates."
- Use-case-focused: "Reduce per-token cost and latency for chat and generation workloads. Built-in observability, model versioning, and enterprise network controls make Redwood ideal for product teams building production LLM features."
4) CTA options (pick one): "Start free trial", "Request demo", "Contact sales"

C. Acceptance QA matrix (check all; NOTE: any "no" -> block unless product owner signs off)
- Metadata & SKUs
  - product_name_short present and <= 80 chars: yes/no
  - product_name_long present and <= 160 chars: yes/no
  - tags <= 10, aligned to allowed taxonomy: yes/no
- Copy compliance
  - No unverified superlatives ("best", "#1") unless benchmark doc attached (link): yes/no
  - No pricing claims that contradict pricing_hint: yes/no
  - Responsible AI & hallucination disclaimers present for generation products: yes/no/na
- Legal & privacy
  - Data handling statement present and matches security page: yes/no
  - KMS/HSM, SOC2/HIPAA flags aligned with product offering: yes/no
- Asset specs
  - Primary tile image 1:1 or 4:3 accepted; min 800px: yes/no
  - Hero image 16:9, min 1200px: yes/no
  - Icon/logo variant provided 128x128: yes/no
- Technical acceptance
  - Integration tested in staging with sample tenant: yes/no/na
  - Billing SKU mapping validated (internal billing id present): yes/no
  - Region availability declared: yes/no
- Launch readiness
  - Trial entitlement config verified in portal: yes/no/na
  - Support contact & escalation path documented: yes/no
  - SLA metrics reviewed and mapped to listing (uptime/response): yes/no/na

D. Creative & image guidelines (bulleted quick rules)
- Visual style: use product screenshots over stylized stock where possible (helps acceptance).
- Include one screenshot labelled with overlay text "Demo" or "Staging" to avoid confusion with customer data.
- Brand lockups: use public logo .svg; do not add third-party marks without permission.
- Accessibility: alt text for every image, high-contrast CTA button in hero shot.
- Locales: if localized assets supplied, name files with language tag (tile_en.png, tile_de.png).

E. Reg flags & escalation notes (shortcuts for fast triage)
- Red flags (auto-block): health claims, medical/financial advice claims, unencrypted data storage claims.
- Legal review required: any customer-data-storage >90d, any resale of models, any external PII processing outside declared regions.
- Security review required: if product exposes KMS/HSM key import to partner.
- Quick escalation steps: file JIRA with label "marketplace-blocker", ping go-to-market #marketplace-channel, include acceptance matrix screenshot.

F. Localization + SEO tips (practical)
- Translate short headline and long description; DO NOT machine-translate marketing claims without review.
- Use region-specific examples in 1–2 additional sentences for long description when relevant.
- Marketplace SEO: include 2–3 buyer-intent keywords in short headline and first sentence of long description.

G. Launch timeline checklist (sprint-sized)
- Day -14: Finalize SKU brief, attach assets, legal/security flags identified
- Day -10: Ops acceptance QA pass or annotated blockers; billing SKU mapping done
- Day -7: Staging listing created; integration smoke tests executed
- Day -3: Creative final assets uploaded; localization in progress
- Day 0: Publish to marketplace (soft launch); monitor metrics for 72h
- Day +7: Post-launch cleanup and update copy based on early telemetry

H. Sample problems & quick remedies (notes from previous launches)
- Problem: Marketplace truncated long descriptions -> Remedy: move critical messaging to first 1–2 sentences and use bullets later.
- Problem: Icon rejected for ratio -> Remedy: supply both 1:1 and transparent svg; keep margin safe zone.
- Problem: Trial entitlement misconfigured -> Remedy: test with a fake org+billing tenant before publish; keep sample account credentials in staging-only Confluence page.

I. TODOs / open questions (notes to self)
- Who owns final pricing copy for multi-cloud SKU variants? (Sales or Product?) -> action: tag @Marcus for decision by 2025-02-07.
- Should we maintain a canonical image set for partner co-branded tiles? (Pros/cons list needed)
- Align "Responsible AI" snippet with R&D/Applied ML recommended language — ping @Leah for final wording.

J. Quick appendices (links & refs)
- Confluence: Marketplace listing style guide (supply id in linked_artifacts)
- Jira template: use JIRA-GO2M-987 for blockers
- Internal PR checklist: repo /website PR for product page updates

Notes to reviewer: keep the doc intentionally compact. This is meant for day-to-day ops and should be copied into partner onboarding packs. If something keeps failing at acceptance, we should promote that check into the mandatory seller brief (i.e., gating field).

-- end --
